# 2004A Question 7 {.unnumbered}

::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} the mechanisms of action of inotropes and [**provide examples**]{.task-verb}.
:::

:::: {#answer-structure}

## Suggested Structure

[**Describe**]{.task-verb} **Beta-1 Agonists**, **Cardiac Glycosides**, and **Phosphodiesterase Inhibitors**, providing examples. [**Define**]{.task-verb} inotropy and connect each mechanism to intracellular calcium and contractility; [**include**]{.task-verb} other relevant inotropes separately.

::::

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
**67%** of candidates passed this question.

Main points expected included:

- Definition of inotropes
- Roles of c-AMP and intracellular Ca^2+^ in promoting cardiac contractility
- Beta-1 agonists, cardiac glycosides, phosphodiesterase inhibitors (III) and their mechanisms of action

Credit was given for mention of glucagon and calcium.

Common errors included:

- Failure to define inotropes or stating that inotropes were agents which increased blood pressure and discussing alpha agonists at length
- Many candidates wrote about sympathomimetic agents or catecholamines including those which act predominantly by vasoconstriction
:::
